heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Polymaker PolyLite ASA exceptionally well out of the box thanks to its fully enclosed build chamber and high-temperature heated bed. With an effective volumetric flow limit of 17 mm³/s, you can reliably run standard outer and inner perimeters up to a calculated safe maximum print speed of 202 mm/s.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of PVP glue stick or liquid adhesive as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap the Max Volumetric Speed at 17.0 mm³/s in the filament settings to eliminate underextrusion during high-speed moves.
Set the auxiliary part cooling fan and chamber exhaust fan to 0% to maintain stable enclosure heat and prevent layer delamination.
Increase Bed Temperature to 98°C for all layers and preheat the chamber to at least 40°C by soaking the bed for 10-15 minutes prior to printing.
Tune Pressure Advance (Linear Advance) specifically to around 0.038 s to avoid corner bulging while preserving sharp edge profiles at 202 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and warping off the build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Thermal contraction caused by low bed temperature, poor first layer adhesion, or cold air drafts inside the chamber.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase bed temperature to 100°C, clean the PEI plate thoroughly with dish soap and water, apply liquid adhesive, and keep the front door and top glass strictly closed.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer cracking and splitting during print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or chamber temperature drop causing high residual thermal stress between printed layers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Lower the part cooling fan range to 10-20%, disable the auxiliary side fan completely (0%), and pre-heat the chamber using the bed heater before starting.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Surface bubbling, rough texture, and excessive stringing
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in the ASA filament causing steam expansion during extrusion inside the nozzle.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated filament dryer or the X1C chamber drying mode at 70°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, and store inside an AMS with fresh desiccant.

faq.question: Can I print Polymaker PolyLite ASA directly from the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, PolyLite ASA spools fit and feed reliably inside the AMS, provided the spool is not deformed and dry desiccant is installed to prevent moisture pickup.

faq.question: Do I need to leave the door or top glass open when printing ASA on the X1C?
faq.answer: No, keep all panels and the front door completely closed to retain heat and prevent thermal shrinkage that causes ASA to warp or delaminate.

faq.question: Why is glue stick recommended on a Textured PEI Plate for ASA?
faq.answer: ASA can chemically fuse to PEI coatings at high bed temperatures; the glue stick acts primarily as an interfacial release agent to protect the build plate from tearing.

faq.question: What is the maximum printing speed I can achieve with PolyLite ASA on the X1C?
faq.answer: Given the maximum volumetric flow rate of 17 mm³/s at 250°C, the calculated safe ceiling speed is 202 mm/s using a standard 0.4mm nozzle at 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width.
